verdict: NOT CONVERGED — AND UNREACHABLE WITHIN THE CAP. Round 4 measured 6 blocking findings (each spot-verified as constructible against surface-v4.md/draft-v4.md; none is a ledger-accepted tradeoff) and 2 novel frictions (both aimed at the one-line -S flag entry), and forced text changes (v5) — the two-consecutive-clean-rounds counter stays at zero. Convergence required rounds 4 AND 5 both to measure 0 blocking / 0 novel friction with no text change on a surface stable at 2 concepts / 1 verb (restore) / 1 flag (--force); round 4 failed that bar and only round 5 remains under the 5-round hard cap, so two consecutive clean rounds no longer fit: convergence cannot be reached within this run. Round 5 should still run as the exit measurement — a freeze-check exercising the six round-4 repairs (owner-unreadable-mode restore-and-verify; folded-target plan/force/no-op outputs; id -s -S closure resolvability through cat, restore pre-flight, and gc; cross-implementation folded listing bytes; unreadable-symlink-target scans and gates; case-fold restores onto default APFS) plus doc-only sims. A clean round 5 leaves v5 exactly one confirmation short of the freeze bar, to be completed outside this run; a dirty round 5 folds as v6. Surface spend remained within budget every round. Honest accounting note: of the 6 blockers, 3 were opened by round-3 repair 2's own new pins, 2 are survivals of condemned defect classes at inputs the round-3 repairs did not cover, and 1 (destination name-folding) is genuinely new — the freeze-check also verified all five round-3 repairs closed on their constructed inputs, so the design is monotonically hardening, just not yet fixed-point.

ledger_additions.item: Restore verification observes interleaved: every field of line 2 is observed from the filesystem in this run, each at the last moment it remains observable — files restore writes are read back and rehashed after sync and before their recorded mode lands; files restore kept were read and hashed by this run's own pre-image scan; modes and mtimes are applied and observed children before parents, each entry's recomputed line settling as its own metadata lands. Applying a recorded mode can never blind verification: snapshots whose recorded modes deny their owner read (minted through group/other permission bits, or by root) restore and verify exit 0. Residue stated in NOTES: a later re-scan, and the pre-image scan of any further restore or undo over that directory, needs read granted first (the completeness gate refuses what it cannot capture); granting it is a mode change the next pre-image records honestly.

ledger_additions.item: Folded sequences fully pinned: the -s ingest stores the ID-list object of every folded sequence entry (fsynced like any listing, before the journal append); a folded entry's ID names its ID list — the member files' IDs, one per line in member order, one object serving both knowledge levels (members are files, whose two IDs coincide); its size is the sum of the member file sizes the scan read and hashed, never the ID-list text's byte length; in full form its mode is the members' shared mode and its mtime is the newest member mtime; a run folds only when every member is a plain file and every observed member mode is equal (non-qualifying files record as ordinary entries); folding happens only under -S; the foldable-run test is fixed by the frozen c4m sequence form, identically in every implementation; restore materializes every member with the entry's one recorded mode and mtime.
ledger_additions.reason: ROUND-4 FREEZE-CHECK BLOCKERS 3 AND 4. The twice-stated exhaustive ingest enumeration included no ID-list object while three consumers (cat Final, restore pre-flight, gc closure) require it from the store — a capability with no producing mechanism, the bar that made round-3 blocker 1 blocking: a literal conforming id -s -S minted a snapshot whose folded entries dangled, falsifying 'the store alone recovers everything'. And the folded entry's size/mode/mtime had multiple faithful readings (the design's own precedents point opposite ways on size), letting conforming scanners mint divergent listing bytes — divergent snapshot AND content IDs — for the same -S scan, resurrecting round-3 blocker 2's symptom one field over.

ledger_additions.item: Symlink-target totality and the incomplete-entry class: a symlink whose target text could not be read records its name and kind, observed mode/mtime in full form, and null target text, null size, null ID (a symlink's read is readlink, and nothing was read); restore keep-as-found and exit 2 own the incomplete-entry class — file or directory entries with null ID, and symlink entries with null target text — while a symlink entry with recorded target text stays complete and is never an omission; the completeness gate names unreadable symlink targets, its symlink sentence scoped to readable target text (broken or not; the target need not exist); a scan attempts every name its parent's listing enumerates, in canonical order; an entry whose kind could not be observed at all is reported and omitted, like sockets/fifos/devices.
ledger_additions.reason: ROUND-4 FREEZE-CHECK BLOCKER 5. Repair 3's 'total for every entry kind' was not total for symlinks: mkdir p; ln -s t p/l; chmod 444 p is single-user constructible on mainstream platforms (readdir shows the link; readlink is refused), no null-target rendering was pinned, so omission, a null-target form, and refusal all read as conforming — the same-tree-same-access-outcome listing divergence the totality rule exists to kill — while the gate sentence 'Symlinks — broken or not — are fully recordable' was simultaneously false behind the gate that guarantees complete capture before destruction. Amends the decided gate sentence under the concrete-defect standard and closes the kind-unobservable and r-without-x attempt-set siblings with the same discipline.
